notes:
I couldn't write any notes this time, because none of the sources came through.

I asked for five pages at once: Enduring Word's Psalm 78 page, Bible Hub's commentaries on 78:25, Augustine on this psalm at New Advent, the NET Bible notes, and Precept Austin's Psalm 78 page. A bug in my own code stopped me from reading what came back, so I don't know if any of the pages loaded. Then the research tool hit its limit for this turn, and I couldn't fix the code or try again.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory.

If you send the request again, I'll start with those five pages. Then I'll go through these, roughly in this order:
- **Verse by verse:** Bible Hub's pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and others), StudyLight, and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*.
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, Grace to You (gty.org), Desiring God and LCMS, for the verses where they may differ. Likely examples are v. 25 ("bread of angels" and manna pointing to Christ), vv. 34–37 (whether that repentance was real) and vv. 38–39 (mercy and wrath).
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, and New Advent for Catholic and Orthodox readings, including Augustine and the Eucharistic reading of v. 25.

I'd also need a higher limit on research steps to get through this many pages in one turn.
